name: Aribwaung
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Read full scanned text of Holzknecht 1989, The Markham languages of Papua New Guinea (PL C-115, ANU repository): Aribwaungg phoneme section (Table 4.14) has no stress statement; only 4 'stress' hits in book, none on Aribwaung.

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request); access check: open copy online; also in print at Harvard (Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6201.R67 1988) (also lendable online at archive.org)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL6201 .R67 1988
sources.note: 'Yalu (= Aribwaungg)' appears only in cognate sets, the a- noun-prefix discussion (ex. 4.3) and consonant-correspondence tables; the eight 'stress' hits concern Ali/Kairiru and Proto-Oceanic reconstruction, none Yalu.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.x languoid page arib1240 (Aribwaung); en.wikipedia 'Aribwaung language'
sources.note: Glottolog cites only Holzknecht 1989 (subclassification comment); Wikipedia reproduces Holzknecht's phoneme table and cites Ethnologue + Holzknecht 1989 only; neither says anything about stress.

sources.citation: Wurm, S.A. (ed.). 1997. Some endangered languages of Papua New Guinea: Kaki Ae, Musom, and Aribwatsa. Pacific Linguistics D-89 (contains Holzknecht, 'Musom morphology and grammar sketch', 69-108, and 'Aribwatsa: a lost language of the Markham family?', 145-163). DOI 10.15144/PL-D89.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Aribwaungg/Yalu mentioned 21 times, only in sociolinguistic history and comparative pronoun/word-order remarks; no phonological description of Aribwaungg. 'Stress is always penultimate' (p. 18) is Clifton's Kaki Ae sketch, not Markham; 'The vowel in the unstressed syllable becomes schwa' (p. 73) is Musom only.

sources.note: One sociolinguistic mention of Aribwaungg (Yalu); nothing on phonology.

sources.citation: Holzknecht, Susanne. 1989. The Markham languages of Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics C-115. Canberra: ANU. viii+228 pp. DOI 10.15144/PL-C115; hdl 1885/145647.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.harvard_location: Widener Library (offsite storage), call number PL5026 .H64 1989
sources.note: Sec. 4.2.13 Aribwaungg, printed pp. 57-58 (PDF pp. 65-66): Table 4.14 phonemes + notes 1-8 on segmental allophony, glottal-stop allophone of /k/, Bukawa loans, rarity of vowel sequences. No statement on stress, accent, tone or prosody. Ch. 4 intro p. 50: 'brief phonological statement.. Full phonological statements are to be published at a later date'. Only four 'stress' hits in the whole book, none on Aribwaungg (dialect-perception remark; Duwet note 11 on unstressed vowel sequences; Watut historical 'through stress rules'; a comparative *e remark).
